html:
The second ecumenical council of the Christian church, called by Theodosius I and held in Constantinople from May to July 381, in the church of Hagia Irene. About 150 bishops came, all from the east.

It closed the long fight over Arianism that followed the Council of Nicaea. It expanded the Nicene Creed, adding that the Holy Spirit is Lord and giver of life, worshipped with the Father and the Son. The result, the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed, is still the creed most churches say today.

It also ruled that the bishop of Constantinople ranked second only to the bishop of Rome, because the city was the new Rome. That ranking set up centuries of rivalry with Alexandria and, later, with Rome itself. The church where it met was later burned and rebuilt by Justinian.
sum: The second ecumenical council of the Christian church, called by Theodosius I and held in Constantinople from May to July 381, in the church of Hagia Irene. About 150 bishops came, all from the east.
